content: The medication sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and citric acid is commonly used to cleanse the intestines prior to surgical procedures or diagnostic tests such as colonoscopies or X-rays. It functions as a laxative by drawing significant amounts of water into the intestines and stimulating the colon, resulting in watery bowel movements (diarrhea). Instructions for Use: 1. Preparation and Administration: Carefully read the Medication Guide and any instructions provided by your doctor or pharmacist before starting this medication. Follow all directions precisely. This product is available as a powder (to be mixed with water) or as a ready-to-drink liquid. If using the powder, mix each dose with 5 ounces (150 mL) of cold water just before use. Take the medication in two separate doses as directed by your doctor. Follow the timing instructions for each dose carefully. 2. Dietary Restrictions: On the day before your procedure, consume only clear liquids. Avoid milk, dairy products, red or dark-colored liquids, and alcohol. To prevent dehydration, drink plenty of clear liquids before, during, and after taking this medication. Include a variety of clear liquids as recommended by your doctor. 3. Timing with Other Medications: Do not take oral medications within one hour of starting this product, as it may interfere with their absorption. Certain medications (e.g., digoxin, iron, tetracycline antibiotics, quinolone antibiotics, chlorpromazine, penicillamine) should not be taken within two hours before or six hours after taking this product. 4. Expected Effects: Watery bowel movements typically begin 2 to 4 hours after taking the medication. This is a normal response and indicates the medication is working. Side Effects: Common side effects include frequent watery bowel movements, nausea, vomiting, bloating, headache, and abdominal cramps. This medication may cause dehydration due to excessive loss of fluids and salts. Serious allergic reactions are rare but may occur. If you experience severe symptoms or suspect an allergic reaction, seek immediate medical attention. Contact your doctor for advice on managing side effects. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you have any allergies or medical conditions before using this medication. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Use during pregnancy should only occur if clearly necessary. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and citric acid may interact with other medications, altering their effectiveness or increasing the risk of side effects. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you are taking and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: In case of overdose with serious symptoms (e.g., fainting, difficulty breathing), call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Storage: Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your pharmacist or local waste disposal guidelines. Additional Information: This summary does not include all possible information about the product. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete details tailored to your specific health needs. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for this medication and any potential risks to the infant. This medication is marketed under brand names such as Clenpiq and Prepopik.
